metodos-de-estudio-que-de-verdad-funcion.titulo: Rereading and highlighting barely work: the review that evaluated 10 study techniques with real evidence
metodos-de-estudio-que-de-verdad-funcion.resumen: A comprehensive review of scientific evidence on study techniques found that self-testing (retrieval practice) and spacing out study sessions over time are the techniques with the highest proven utility, while rereading and highlighting, the most popular methods, yield poor results.

cuanto-tiempo-toma-formar-un-habito.titulo: How long does it actually take to form a healthy habit? (It's not 21 days)
cuanto-tiempo-toma-formar-un-habito.resumen: A meta-analysis of 20 studies involving 2,601 people found that health habits take an average of 59 to 154 days to form, with enormous variability from person to person, far from the popular "21 days" myth.

practica-deliberada-cuanto-explica-la-ex.titulo: Deliberate practice: how much it really explains skill mastery, according to the meta-analysis that put Ericsson to the test
practica-deliberada-cuanto-explica-la-ex.resumen: A meta-analysis re-analysing the evidence behind Anders Ericsson's theory of deliberate practice found that the amount of practice explains a substantial portion of performance in games and music, but very little in professions and education, far from the "practice explains almost everything" idea popularised by the 10,000-hour rule.

mentalidad-de-crecimiento-que-dice-la-ev.titulo: "Growth mindset" is not magic: what a study with 12,000 students and two meta-analyses actually found
mentalidad-de-crecimiento-que-dice-la-ev.resumen: The idea that believing intelligence can be developed improves performance has real evidence behind it, but the effect is small and concentrated in certain students, not the universal solution usually sold.

procrastinacion-productividad-estudianti.titulo: Almost all of us procrastinate: what really explains why we delay tasks and how it relates to performance
procrastinacion-productividad-estudianti.resumen: A meta-analysis covering over 20 years of research found that procrastination is mainly explained by low self-efficacy and impulsivity, rather than laziness, and that it is consistently associated with lower academic performance.

como-aprendemos-estrategias-metacognitiv.titulo: Learning how to learn: why teaching metacognitive strategies improves performance (with caveats)
como-aprendemos-estrategias-metacognitiv.resumen: A meta-analysis found that training students in learning strategies and metacognition improves academic performance with a moderate effect, but this effect is larger when delivered by a researcher than when implemented by a regular teacher in the everyday classroom.

clase-magistral-vs-aprendizaje-activo-me.titulo: The traditional lecture loses out: the meta-analysis of 225 studies comparing passive lecturing with active participation
clase-magistral-vs-aprendizaje-activo-me.resumen: A meta-analysis of 225 studies in science, technology, engineering, and mathematics found that students in traditional lecture classes are 1.5 times more likely to fail than those taught using active learning methods, and score worse on exams on average.

aprendizaje-en-linea-vs-presencial.titulo: Online learning: the key is not the screen, it is how it is used
aprendizaje-en-linea-vs-presencial.resumen: A meta-analysis of 45 studies found that purely online learning did not outperform face to face learning, but blended learning did, clearly and consistently.
